evals.prompt: Use the task-decomposition skill. Decompose epic 'Multi-tenant support' (currently 21 points) for TaskFlow. Must include data isolation, per-tenant billing, per-tenant branding, admin tenant switcher. Break into stories that fit in a 2-week sprint. List each story with its points and acceptance criteria, and show the create call that attaches it to the epic. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: 4-6 vertical stories each ≤8 points, created in Plane with parent set to the epic, total ≈21, each with user story format + acceptance criteria. Uses Split by Business Rule or Split by Workflow Step pattern.
expectations: The answer splits the epic vertically and not by architecture layer
The answer keeps every story at 8 points or less
The answer makes the story points add up to about 21
The answer writes the acceptance criteria as Given/when/then lines in description_html
The answer creates each story with workitem(action=create, parent=<epic work item id>)
The answer verifies the split with workitem(action=list, pql='childOf("<epic identifier>")')

evals.prompt: Use the task-decomposition skill. Split this 13-point story: 'User can manage their profile' — covers viewing, editing name/bio, uploading picture, and deleting account. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Uses Split by Workflow Step pattern, produces 3-4 children summing to ~13 points, each a vertical slice.
expectations: The answer recognizes this as Split by Workflow Step pattern
The answer says to create 3-4 child stories (view / edit name+bio / upload picture / delete account)
In the answer the child points sum to ~13 (preservation rule)
In the answer each child is a vertical slice (not split by FE/BE/DB layers)
The answer says to create children in Plane with workitem(action=create, parent=<original id>) and can list them back with pql childOf("<identifier>")

evals.prompt: Use the task-decomposition skill. Someone split 'Build signup flow' into: (1) Create users DB schema, (2) Build auth API endpoints, (3) Build signup UI. Review this decomposition. In this session you have no Plane tools and no shell, only file reading and a text answer: say which Plane MCP calls you would make (resource(action=..., ...) with their parameters), in what order, and what you would check, and show the result you would give me.
evals.expected_output: Rejects — this is a horizontal (layer-based) slice. None of the three deliver value alone and all depend on each other. Recommend splitting by feature/behavior instead.
expectations: The answer identifies this as the horizontal slicing anti-pattern
The answer explains that none of the 3 pieces deliver value independently
The answer says to fail INVEST 'Independent' and 'Valuable' criteria
The answer suggests vertical alternative: signup with happy path → validation errors → email verification

evals.prompt: Use the task-decomposition skill. Validate this user story against INVEST: 'As a support agent, I want to flag tickets, so that I can follow up later' — 21 points, no acceptance criteria, depends on a new tags system being built first. Go through every INVEST criterion with a PASS or FAIL verdict and say what to do about each failure. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Fails Small (21 pts), Testable (no AC), and Independent (blocked by tags system). Specific remediation for each.
expectations: The answer says to check each INVEST criterion individually
The answer reports Small: FAIL (21 pts > 8), split required
The answer reports Testable: FAIL (no acceptance criteria), write Given/When/Then
The answer reports Independent: FAIL (blocked by tags system), either wait or scope it in
The answer does NOT just say 'looks good'
